newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says reaction to Zaire proposal positive.
newsitem.headline: France says reaction to Zaire proposal positive.

text.p: France has received positive international reaction to its call for a multinational force to guarantee the safety of refugees in eastern Zaire, French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Tuesday.
He told Reuters during a Franco-Spanish summit in this Mediterranean port city that the reaction had been "rather positive...from everybody".
"The Americans are interested in the Franco-Spanish initiative," he said.

France and Spain called for talks on sending a temporary international force to guarantee the safety of more than one million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees set on the move by fighting in eastern Zaire.
Their call was made after contacts with other countries in the European Union, officials said.
Both said they were prepared to participate in such an operation.
In Washington, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Monday the United States was studying the proposals but needed France to clarify them.

"What we're proposing is that the international community -- Europe, the United States, African states -- organise so that there is a security force on the ground to guarantee people's safety," de Charette said on Monday

Some U.S. officials said it would be hard for Washington to refuse to participate, given its push for an all-Africa crisis response force that could handle such crises in the future. But the Pentagon was said to be cool to a U.S. role in Zaire.
